cs-linearizability.title: A read after the acknowledgment must see the write
cs-linearizability.description: A timeline where a write runs from t=10 to t=30, a read overlapping it may see either value, a read at t=40 must see the new value, and a lagging replica returning the old value breaks the guarantee.
cs-linearizability.note: Once a write completes, no later read may return the older value.

items.title: B reads, overlapping
items.detail: t=15: may see old or new

cs-cap.title: Two choices in a partition, two without one
cs-cap.description: During a partition a cut-off node either refuses requests or answers with possibly stale data. On a healthy network, writes either wait for remote replicas or return early and risk losing recent data.
cs-cap.note: CAP covers only the partition case; the healthy case trades latency against freshness.

cs-ordering.title: Wall clocks can reverse cause and effect
cs-ordering.description: A node with a fast clock stamps an earlier write higher than a later write on an accurate node, so last-write-wins drops the later write, while Lamport counters keep the two in causal order.
cs-ordering.note: A counter carried on each message keeps causally later writes later.

cs-fencing.title: A paused leader wakes up after losing its lease
cs-fencing.description: P1 takes a lease with token 71 and pauses, the lease expires and P2 gets token 72 and writes, P1 wakes believing it still leads, and storage rejects its write because 71 is below 72.
cs-fencing.note: Storage enforces safety, because the paused process cannot know it is stale.

cs-raft.title: A committed entry survives a change of leader
cs-raft.description: In a five-node group, the term 7 leader stores entry 42 on a majority of three, a partition cuts the leader off, a node missing the entry cannot gather a majority, and a node holding it wins term 9.
cs-raft.note: Any two majorities share a node, so a winner cannot lack a committed entry.

cs-2pc.title: Atomic commit, consensus, and where each fits
cs-2pc.description: Two-phase commit needs every participant, consensus needs a majority, running 2PC over consensus groups survives a coordinator crash, and a coordination service packages consensus for small data.
cs-2pc.note: Use a tested coordination service rather than writing your own consensus.

items.title: Two-phase commit
items.detail: all must vote yes; can block
